row3.text: Other states of the description view

s0.text: 1. Start here. You enter the ISBN from the item in hand. LC has a CIP description of this publication, so choose Start from this description.

s1.text: 2. The CIP description names Mark Twain as text only. The editor looks the name up across Blue Core, LC, Wikidata, and FAST. Choose the first result to link it.

s2.text: 3. The description, with Twain linked. Try the Hints toggle and the changes button. Then: Open in the Context box (step 4), Add genre/form (step 5), Find authority for the introducer (step 6), or Add field (step 7).

s3.text: 4. Blue Core already has this Work, with 37 Instances. Use this Work attaches the new publication to it instead of making a duplicate. Edit in Blue Core, by the LC name, leads to step 8.

s4.text: 5. From Add genre/form in the description. The genre describes the shared Work, so the editor asks whether the change should reach all 38 Instances.

s5.text: 6. From Find authority on the introducer. No source has Dana Okafor, so you create a new person in Blue Core, filled in from the item.

s6.text: 7. From Add field. Typing a MARC tag finds the property; suggestions come from how LC describes print monographs.

s7.text: 8. From Edit in Blue Core in the context panel. Adding a variant to Twain's LC name creates a Blue Core version; then the editor offers to move the 214 other descriptions that use LC's version.

s8.text: The hints explainer, opened from the ? next to Hints. It also opens by itself the first time someone uses the editor.

s9.text: The edit history, opened from 3 unsaved changes. Each change can be undone.

s10.text: Hints off: no MARC tags, Work and Instance badges, or MARC preview.
